label: r4c1
name: stem-pooled done/value, 3 epochs
hypothesis: The r2c3 network and recipe, but the DONE and value heads also get the mean and max over cells of the 1x1 stem features. These carry the aligned missing/extra cells for each layer, so 'any target cell still missing?' becomes nearly linear. That should stop early DONE and improve the critic. Refuted if the mean is not above 0.94 or a seed falls below 0.85.
last_analysis: An x-shifted copy of the observation fixed a fixed X/2 misalignment between target channels and action coordinates (0 → 0.59). The stem-feature skip into the footprint head gave the best result (r2c3, 0.94). Recipe: 128 envs with 2–3 epochs beat the default, and batches of 1,024 collapsed to DONE. Runs are fragile: single seeds fell to 0.15 (r1c3, r3c1) and 0.45 (r3c2), so 2 vs 3 epochs is within noise. The weak r3c1 seed stopped too early (IoU 0.83, almost no cells outside the target, training success flat near 0.2); the weak r3c3 seed placed wrong cells. My guess: the DONE and value heads see only pooled post-3x3 features and do not reliably know whether target cells are still missing. Giving them pooled per-cell stem features (which carry missing/extra cells directly) should make stopping reliable and improve the critic. All three candidates add this, each with a different recipe.
